articles.title: Rupee closes at seven-month high of 93.69 as FPI inflows, lower crude prices boost sentiment
articles.excerpt:
The Indian rupee strengthened to a seven-month closing high against the US dollar on Wednesday, supported by foreign inflows and lower crude oil prices. | Photo Credit: iStockphoto

Buoyed by robust FPI inflows into the equity markets and a decline in crude oil prices, the Rupee closed Wednesday near a seven-month high.

The Indian currency closed at 93.69 per US Dollar, up 24 paise over the previous close of 93.93. Intraday, it tested a high/low of 93.62/93.87.

articles.title: Rupee rises 7 paise to close at 93.70 against US dollar
articles.excerpt:
The rupee gained 7 paise to close at 93.70 (provisional) against the US dollar on Wednesday, driven by domestic market strength and foreign capital inflows, alongside potential support from declining global crude oil prices.

Forex traders said the Indian rupee gained as domestic markets rose to an eight-month high amid FPI inflows and easing crude oil prices. However, a strong dollar and a surge in US Treasury yields capped sharp gains.

The dollar strengthened on hotter-than-expected CPI inflation in the US, raising odds of a rate hike by the Fed in December.

articles.title: Rupee touches strongest since April as foreign inflows offset firm dollar
articles.excerpt:
On Wednesday, the Indian rupee surged to its healthiest value since April, closing at 93.69 against the dollar. This upswing was driven by a remarkable influx of foreign investments in local stocks, totaling nearly $6 billion in November. Even in light of a stronger dollar amid US inflation signals, the rupee stood firm. There's a notable optimistic shift in market sentiment, now eager for India's inflation data anticipated for October.

articles.title: Nifty closes 0.84% higher, cooling off from intraday highs
articles.excerpt:
Markets reopened after the Diwali break with a bang on Wednesday, but couldn’t hold on.

The Nifty 50 surged to an intraday high of 25,424, before giving back nearly half its gains as hotter-than-expected US inflation data revived fears of an aggressive Federal Reserve rate hike in December, pulling the index to close at 25,255.05, up 210.40 points or 0.84 per cent.

The Sensex settled at 81,879.40, gaining 772.75 points or 0.95 per cent, well below the 1,300-point surge seen in early trade.

articles.title: Top Yen Forecaster Predicts 147 Per Dollar as Rate Gap Narrows
articles.excerpt:

Now, the top dollar-yen forecaster in Bloomberg’s latest rankings sees the Japanese currency rallying toward 147 per dollar next year as Japan’s interest-rate gap with the US narrows.
